elements.element: Vendor shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with a limit of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The redlined clause does not require commercial general liability insurance.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with an aggregate limit of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The redlined clause does not require commercial general liability insurance or an aggregate limit.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance with a limit of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause requires professional liability insurance of only USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, Vendor shall maintain cyber/privacy liability insurance with a limit of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause requires cyber liability insurance unconditionally, but its limit is only USD 2,000,000 rather than USD 5,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: The redlined clause contains no workers' compensation insurance requirement.

elements.element: Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance upon request.
elements.evidence: The redlined clause contains no obligation to provide certificates of insurance.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance with a limit of at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Kubient to maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor shall maintain cyber liability insurance with a limit of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Kubient to maintain cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.

result.reason: The operative addition exactly reaches the fallback by imposing the required USD 1 million E&O and USD 2 million cyber limits on Kubient. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits commercial general liability, workers' compensation, and certificates on request, and provides lower E&O and cyber limits. The change is narrow and does not disturb the existing general-provisions language.
